quizName:
Hardest Questions in Virginia
									  					
									  														  					Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol harm your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident and silly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, reduces coordination and balance, and makes it hard to judge distance and react to what's around you.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not worry about it because all vehicles are the same.
Not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes before driving to learn where all the vehicle's controls are and how they work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes before driving to learn where all the vehicle's controls are and how they work.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to find and learn the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: Cell phones are a serious source of driver distraction.
questions.explanation: While driving, do not use cell phones, computers, or other distracting devices unless reporting a crash or emergency. Keep your full attention on the road.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Circular signs mark railroad crossings. This sign tells you that a railroad crossing is ahead and you should watch for trains.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign means U-turns are not allowed where it is posted.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate closes.
Not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: Orange signs are used in construction work zones to communicate with drivers.
questions.explanation: Most work zone signs are orange and diamond-shaped, though some are rectangular. These signs and traffic devices are usually reflective so drivers can see them at night.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: These parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
This lane is reserved for buses and vehicles with a driver and at least one passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: If you are in a crash, you must:

options.text: Stop at the crash scene or as close as possible without blocking traffic.
Report the crash to police as soon as possible.
Tell your insurance company right away.

questions.explanation: If you are in a crash, stop at the scene (or as close as you can without blocking traffic). Help anyone who is injured. Report the crash to police right away. Exchange information with other people involved. Tell your insurance company immediately.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even when no other cars are visible.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even when no other cars are visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from the curb. Do not skip signaling. It is a habit you must follow every time.

questions.question: This sign shows:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: Your license will be revoked or suspended if you:

options.text: Take a driver license test for someone else.

questions.explanation: The DMV or a court can revoke or suspend your license if you are convicted of certain crimes. These include lying to the DMV, running from police, and taking a driver license test for another person.

questions.question: Your driver license will be revoked or suspended if you are convicted of:

options.text: Driving while under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
Committing a felony with a motor vehicle.

questions.explanation: The DMV or a court may suspend or revoke your license if you are convicted of certain crimes. These include driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, lying to the DMV, and committing a felony with a motor vehicle.

questions.question: Before changing lanes:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers your plan. Look for other drivers who may also be moving into that lane.

questions.question: Drivers are responsible for keeping children properly secured in vehicles.
questions.explanation: A driver must ensure that anyone under 18 is properly secured with a safety belt, booster seat, or child safety seat. This applies no matter where the child sits in the vehicle.

questions.question: Distracted driving may be caused by:

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. Your full attention is needed for safe driving. Any other activity can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: When driving near light rail vehicles, always:

options.text: Expect trains on any track at any time.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signs.
Be careful turning across train tracks.

questions.explanation: When driving near light rail, expect trains at any time. Obey all signs and traffic signals. Look both ways before crossing train tracks. Only cross if you have room to do so without stopping and can clear the tracks safely.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: When stopped, you must show your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You are required to have all three documents in your vehicle when driving.

questions.question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly from your current lane.
Keep driving until you find the next safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you find the next safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a traffic regulation sign. It tells drivers that left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means it is not safe to enter the road or driveway from your direction. Turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: Drivers should stay a safe distance away from cyclists.
questions.explanation: Drivers must be careful around cyclists and keep a safe distance between their vehicle and the cyclist.

questions.question: Every time you drive, you:
questions.explanation: When you drive, you accept responsibility for your actions. You must follow Virginia's traffic laws and keep yourself, your passengers, and others on the road safe.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause a crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns drivers that cyclists may cross the road.

questions.question: Driving ability can be impaired by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires being in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness can all impair your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, on curves, near pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs tell drivers they must stop and check for traffic before proceeding. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must and must not do. This sign tells you that you cannot park here.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal three to four seconds before you turn. This warns other drivers of your plans.

questions.question: It's your responsibility to ensure that the vehicle you are driving is:
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be registered, and you must carry the registration card while driving. Your vehicle must have insurance. You must make sure the vehicle is safe for you, your passengers, and other drivers on the road.

questions.question: For your own protection, do not:

options.text: Use a suspended or revoked driver license.
Allow an unlicensed driver to operate your vehicle.

questions.explanation: If your license is suspended or revoked, you cannot drive. It is illegal to drive without a valid license. Never lend your license to anyone or let someone without a license drive your car.

questions.question: When obtaining your driver license, DMV may test your:
questions.explanation: The DMV will test your vision. You may also take a knowledge test and a road skills test. A DMV representative will tell you which tests you need to take.
